Subject: Post-demo: resiliency tradeoffs vs hyperscalers — validation plan & test asks

Tom — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap and the specific tests we propose to validate where Redwood differs from hyperscaler-hosted inference endpoints.

Recap highlights:
- Smart routing + model fallbacks: we can route by latency/cost and automatically fallback to a compatible model variant in another region when a node pool is degraded.
- Prefix/KV caching: reduces token cost and p50 latency for repeated prompts; hyperscalers typically lack transparent KV cache for sequence reuse.
- Cost-aware throttles: per-route batching and token-based throttles to keep unit economics predictable under burst.

Proposed validation plan (short, executable):
1) Steady throughput run (24h): 50 req/s average (100k tokens/min peak) — capture p50/p95/p99 latency and error rate.
2) Regional failover probe: simulate 30s of degraded node capacity in primary region and validate successful routing to fallback within 30s and traffic recovery behavior.
3) Burst + rate-limit recovery: 5x traffic spike for 2 minutes, then return to baseline — measure throttling, error budgets, and how quickly the system recovers.

Success criteria (draft):
- Steady p95 <= 350ms for targeted prompts
- Failover: 99% of traffic served within 2s of failover window start
- Burst recovery: error rate < 2% during spike and restoration to <0.5% within 60s

Attachments: resilience_validation_matrix.xlsx (test matrix + scripts). Can you confirm the proposed test windows (preferred: Sept 1–3) and point me to the infra contact we should coordinate with? Also flag any constraints (maintenance windows, IP allowlisting) we should know about.

Thanks — we'll have Soojin scope the probe scripts and Marissa loop in customer success for runbook handoff.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi Tom — quick technical answers to your bullets:

- p95 target and sequence length: for 600-token sequences p95 ~350–450ms is typical on our optimized 80GB A100 pools with warm KV cache. If you expect a cold KV fetch rate >30% latency will skew higher; we'll include cache-warmup steps in the test plan.

- S3-like outage simulation: yes — we can run a controlled artifact store failure for the region by introducing a temporary rate-limit/latency on model artifact fetch paths. The failover path will attempt to route to a compatible quantized variant in the fallback region; expect cold-start penalty ~150–300ms + network delta.

- Deliverables: post-test we'll provide anonymized request logs (JSONL), aggregated latency histograms, per-model error rates, traces for the failover window, and a short runbook with remediation suggestions.

- Pricing for burst: for the pilot we can cover up to 24 hours of test traffic under pilot credits. Any extended recurring burst patterns beyond pilot will be billed per our hosted API rate card. We'll confirm in the SoW.

Attached: failover_probe_script.sh (probe harness), kv_cache_test_plan.md (cache warmup steps & sampling).

I'll prepare a brief runbook and schedule a 30-minute pre-test call with your infra team to walk through IPs, allowlists, and any VPC peering.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer
